# Editor

109 tools. Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_component_to_actor`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Attach a new component of a given class to an actor ALREADY PLACED in the level (an instance-level component, not a change to its Blueprint -- for that use add_component_to_blueprint, which affects every instance). Returns object_path, the full reflection path to feed straight into set_properties / call_function to configure it, so no dedicated add_* wrapper is needed. Pass idempotent=true to make re-running safe. Editor world only; the change dirties the actor's package, so save_level to keep it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Name of the placed actor to add the component to (editor world). |
| `component_type` | string | yes | Component class name (e.g., 'StaticMeshComponent', 'BoxComponent', 'UStaticMeshComponent') |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name to assign to the new component |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] relative location (for scene components) |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation (for scene components) |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] relative scale (for scene components) |
| `idempotent` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false). When true, if the actor already has a component of this class, return it instead of adding a duplicate (already_existed:true). Use for single-instance components. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name: string, component_name: string, object_path: string, requested_component_name: string, component_type: string, already_existed: bool, success: bool }`

## `add_enum_entry`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Append one enumerator to a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum) and give it a display name.  Idempotent (an entry whose display/internal name already exists reports already_existed with added=false, leaving the enum unchanged -- the engine itself does NOT dedup). The new entry lands at the end, before the hidden _MAX sentinel.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum). |
| `entry_name` | string | yes | Display name for the new enumerator. |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, entry_name: string, added: bool, already_existed: bool, entry_count: int, entries: [string] }`

## `add_message_log_entry`

*Additive.*

Add one message to a named editor Message Log listing (for example "PIE", "MapCheck" or a new name, created on demand) at Info, Warning or Error severity; an unrecognised severity becomes Info, and a missing log_name or message is an error. Entries stay in memory for the editor session and are never saved. Use it for diagnostics meant for Window > Message Log; print_to_output_log writes to the Output Log instead. message_count is the listing's message count after the add. Read entries back with get_message_log_entries, show the window with open_message_log, empty the listing with clear_message_log.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log_name` | string | yes | The message log listing name (e.g. "PIE", "MapCheck", or a custom name). |
| `message` | string | yes | The message text to add. |
| `severity` | string | no | EMessageSeverity token: "Info" (default), "Warning", "Error". |

**Returns:** `{ added: bool, log_name: string, message: string, severity: string, message_count: int }`

## `add_struct_member`

*Additive.*

Add a field to a Blueprint (user-defined) struct: the way to grow a data shape -- a DataTable row struct, a save record, a component's payload -- without opening the struct editor. Honest on collisions: if the new name is invalid or already used it ROLLS BACK the auto-named member it had to create first and returns an error, instead of reporting success under the engine's MemberVar_N name and leaving orphans behind. Adding a field to a struct a DataTable already uses changes every row (new field at its default), so re-read the table afterwards. get_struct_members lists what is there; rename_struct_member and remove_struct_member are the edits.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `struct_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the struct (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyStruct). |
| `member_name` | string | yes | New member name. |
| `member_type` | string | yes | Type string resolved through the Blueprint pin-type resolver: scalars (bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte), plus struct/enum/class/object types addressed by name or asset path. An unresolvable string is an error, not a silent default. |

**Returns:** `{ struct_path, member_name, member_type, member_count }`

## `align_actors`

*Destructive.*

Snap two or more editor-world actors onto a shared location, rotation and/or scale taken from a reference (the first, the last, their average, or a named actor). Use it to straighten a hand-placed row or make a set of props share an orientation, in one undoable step; set_actor_transforms is the tool when each actor needs a DIFFERENT transform. WARNING: aligning "location" collapses them onto the same point -- for a row, align only rotation/scale and set positions yourself.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_names` | array | yes | Array of at least 2 INTERNAL actor names (GetName) in the editor world; fewer is an error, and editor labels do not resolve. |
| `align_type` | string | no | "location" (default), "rotation", "scale" or "all" -- which transform components get copied from the reference. |
| `reference` | string | no | Where the target values come from: "first" (default), "last", "average" (the componentwise mean of all of them), or the internal name of one of the listed actors. |

**Returns:** `{ aligned_count: int, align_type: string, reference: string, aligned_actors: [actor JSON] }`

## `begin_transaction`

*Destructive.*

Open one undoable transaction so a whole batch of edits collapses into a SINGLE undo entry: every Modify() between this and end_transaction joins it, and cancel_transaction rolls the lot back without leaving anything on the stack. Use it to make a multi-step edit atomically reversible; the returned transaction_index is what end_transaction / cancel_transaction need. already_open:true means one was already running -- transactions do not nest here.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | string | no | Label shown in the editor's undo history (e.g. 'MCP: retag turrets'). Make it recognisable; it is what get_transaction_history and next_undo report. |
| `primary_object_path` | string | no | Optional object path recorded as the transaction's PrimaryObject, so the undo entry is attributable to one asset/actor. |

**Returns:** `{ description: string, transaction_index: int, already_open: bool, undo_count: int }`

## `cancel_transaction`

*Destructive.*

Abort the transaction opened by begin_transaction: the edits made inside it are rolled back and NO entry is written to the undo stack (undo_count is unchanged). The escape hatch when a multi-step edit goes wrong halfway -- cleaner than committing with end_transaction and then calling undo, which leaves history behind.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ success: bool, transaction_index: int (the one that was cancelled), undo_count: int (unchanged -- nothing was recorded) }`

## `capture_high_res_screenshot`

*Destructive.*

Capture a high-resolution (supersampled) screenshot and write it to a PNG SYNCHRONOUSLY. Prefers the Play-In-Editor game view when PIE is active (captured_pie=true); otherwise the active editor viewport. Drives FViewport::TakeHighResScreenShot() + FViewport::Draw(), which renders at resolution_multiplier x the viewport size and blocks (via ProcessScreenShots) until the file is on disk. The "HighResShot" exec path defers the write to the next render frame, which never runs headless, so it writes nothing. Requires a real RHI (errors honestly under -nullrhi) and a live viewport. Note: the supersampled path re-renders the scene, so the UMG/Slate HUD is NOT included; use capture_pie_screenshot for a HUD-inclusive PIE shot.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resolution_multiplier` | number | no | Resolution multiplier (clamped 1..16, default 2). |
| `filename` | string | no | Optional output path; a bare name lands under &lt;ProjectSaved>/Screenshots/, an absolute path is respected verbatim. ".png" is appended if missing. Defaults to a timestamped name. |

**Returns:** `{ written: bool, file_path: string, resolution_multiplier: int, width: int, height: int, captured_pie: bool }`

## `capture_viewport`

*Destructive.*

Screenshot the active editor viewport to a PNG (forcing a fresh draw first), optionally resized and optionally returned inline as base64. Use it to SHOW a result -- proof that something looks right, an image to hand to a human. Do NOT use it to diagnose: an image costs far more context than a command and is read far less reliably than one, so for "is the actor there / did the value change / did it move" prefer get_actor_bounds, get_component_properties, raycast_scene or a property read, which answer exactly and cheaply. Captures the EDITOR viewport, not a PIE window; capture_high_res_screenshot is the higher-resolution sibling.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | number | no | Optional target width to downscale/upscale to (omit to keep native viewport size). |
| `height` | number | no | Optional target height (only used when width is also supplied). |
| `filename` | string | no | Optional output filename (default MCP_Capture_&lt;timestamp>.png); ".png" extension is added if missing. |
| `return_base64` | boolean | no | bool, also include image_base64 + image_format in the response (default false). |

**Returns:** `{ file_path: string, width: int, height: int, byte_size: int, image_base64: string, image_format: string }`

## `consolidate_assets`

*Destructive.*

Redirect every reference to the source assets onto the target with UEditorAssetSubsystem::ConsolidateAssets, which DELETES the sources (leaving redirectors) and saves what it changed. Only class-compatible sources are used; others are listed in skipped_incompatible and unloadable ones are dropped silently. dry_run=true only reports.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target_asset_path` | string | yes | The asset to keep, all references point here |
| `source_asset_paths` | array | yes | Assets to consolidate into the target |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | If true, skip ConsolidateAssets entirely and only report what would happen, default false |

**Returns:** `dry_run=true: { target_asset_path, target_class, dry_run: true, would_consolidate: [string], skipped_incompatible: [{path,class}], compatible_count: int, incompatible_count: int }; dry_run=false (default): { target_asset_path, target_class, dry_run: false, consolidated_count: int, source_count: int, success: bool, skipped_incompatible: [{path,class}], incompatible_count: int }`

## `create_blueprint_interface`

*Destructive.*

Create a Blueprint Interface asset: a contract of function signatures that unrelated classes can implement, so callers talk to the contract instead of a concrete class. The right tool when several different kinds of actor must answer the same request (interactable, damageable, workable) and you do not want a shared base class -- one interface replaces N-by-M hard-wired cases. Created empty: add functions with add_blueprint_function, then implement_interface on each class and add_blueprint_function with override=true per function.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (no path) |
| `path` | string | no | Target content path for the new asset (default /Game/Blueprints) |

**Returns:** `{ name, path, type }`

## `create_enum`

*Additive.*

Create a Blueprint enum asset from an ordered list of enumerator DISPLAY names -- states, categories and types that Blueprints and DataTable columns switch on. Errors if the asset already exists (not idempotent). Beware the display/internal split that follows: the engine stores enumerators internally as NewEnumerator0, NewEnumerator1, ... and writers into DataTables must use those internal names, because a display name containing spaces is cut at the first space by the text importer and silently lands on index 0. So keep single-word display names, or expect to write NewEnumeratorN. add_enum_entry / rename_enum_entry / reorder_enum_entry edit it afterwards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Enum asset name. |
| `entries` | array | yes | Ordered list of enumerator display-name strings. |
| `path` | string | no | Target content path for the new asset (default /Game/Blueprints) |

**Returns:** `{ name, path, entry_count }`

## `delete_actor`

*Destructive.*

Remove one actor from the EDITOR level through the editor's own delete path (select + edactDeleteSelected), so it is transacted and undoable, and echo back the deleted actor's JSON. WARNING: two edges that bite: it matches the INTERNAL name only -- unlike set_actor_transform, an editor LABEL will not resolve -- and it clears the current selection as a side effect. It cannot touch PIE actors (editor world only), and the deletion lives in memory until save_level writes the .umap. Use delete_actors for several at once.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Actor's internal name (GetName), case-insensitive but WHOLE-string. Editor labels are NOT accepted here; resolve one first with find_actors_by_name. |

**Returns:** `{ deleted_actor: actor JSON captured before the delete }`

## `delete_actors`

*Destructive.*

Delete several editor-world actors at once through the editor's own delete path, in ONE undoable transaction (a single undo brings them all back), returning the count and the JSON of each actor captured before deletion. WARNING: matches INTERNAL names only -- editor labels do not resolve -- names it cannot find are skipped silently, so compare deleted_count against how many you asked for; and if NONE resolve it errors with "No actors found to delete". Editor world only, and the removal is in memory until save_level writes the .umap.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_names` | array | yes | Array of internal actor names (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Unmatched entries are dropped without an error; resolve labels first with find_actors_by_name. |

**Returns:** `{ deleted_count: int (compare against your input length), deleted_actors: [actor JSON captured before the delete] }`

## `delete_assets`

*Destructive.*

GUARDED batch asset deletion. ***dry_run DEFAULTS TO TRUE*** (deliberate: it is the most destructive command in the plugin, `delete_assets(["/Game/VendorPack"], recursive=true)` would be a valid unconfirmed call, and agent allowlists may run mutating tools with no prompt). Four independent gates REFUSE per item instead of skipping silently: readonly_roots (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots), protect_paths (wildcards -- the only gate that saves a zero-referencer asset), the currently-open editor world, and the OPT-IN require_zero_referencers gate whose referencer count EXCLUDES referencers that are themselves in this batch (so a self-contained dead subgraph can still be deleted whole). Deletion is a single ObjectTools::ForceDeleteObjects over the whole eligible batch -- resolving each object here via StaticFindObject/StaticLoadObject rather than through UEditorAssetSubsystem::DeleteAsset, whose UE::EditorAssetUtils::LoadAssetFromPath/EnsureAssetsLoaded preamble is a known crash site ("Array index out of bounds", deterministic on corrupted leftovers). deleted_count counts ONLY items that passed BOTH post-delete probes -- the package file is gone (FPackageName::DoesPackageExist) AND the object no longer resolves at its original path (StaticFindObject) -- never the API's own return value. Both are required because for a never-saved, registry-visible asset the disk probe is vacuously true (it was never on disk), so residency is the only real evidence; each failure names which probe still sees the item.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_paths` | array | yes | List of asset paths (or folder paths when recursive is true). Required, non-empty. |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | If true, expand folder paths to all contained assets. Default false. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | Default TRUE. Nothing is deleted; would_delete reports what WOULD go, with each item's gate verdict. Pass false to actually delete. |
| `readonly_roots` | array | no | Content roots that may never be deleted from. Default: the project's Read Only Content Roots; pass [] to disable the gate entirely. Matches are REFUSED (refused_readonly_root), never silently skipped. (Read via mcp_common::ParseReadonlyRoots, so the type is declared here.) |
| `protect_paths` | array | no | Wildcard patterns (FString::MatchesWildcard, case-insensitive, `*` spans '/') matched against both the package name and the object path. Default [] (gate off). Matches are REFUSED (refused_protected). |
| `require_zero_referencers` | boolean | no | Default FALSE. When true, an asset with at least one referencer OUTSIDE this batch is refused. The per-item external_referencer_count is reported either way. |
| `dependency_type` | string | no | Referencer filter for the count above: "hard"\|"soft"\|"all" (case-insensitive), default "all". |

**Returns:** `{ requested_count, expanded_count, recursive, dry_run, readonly_roots: [string], protect_paths: [string], require_zero_referencers: bool, dependency_type: string, expanded_folders: [{folder, asset_count}], eligible_count, would_delete: [{path, package_name, external_referencer_count, external_referencers: [string], on_disk}], deleted: [{path, package_name, deleted, still_loaded, error?}], deleted_count, failed_count, force_delete_reported_count, refused_readonly_root: [{path, matched_root}], refused_protected: [{path, matched_pattern}], refused_referenced: [{path, external_referencer_count, external_referencers: [string]}], refused_open_world: [{path, reason}], refused_count, results: [{path, success, error}], note, verification: {...} }`

## `delete_directory`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

DESTRUCTIVE: removes a content-browser folder AND every asset inside it, recursively, with no dry-run and no referencer check (unlike delete_assets, which defaults to dry_run and refuses vendored roots). Driven through UEditorAssetSubsystem, which is the pair that works headless. Idempotent: an already-absent folder answers already_absent:true. Verify afterwards with `git status` on the corresponding Content/ path -- never with the `deleted` flag alone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | UE long path of the folder to delete, e.g. /Game/Scratch. Must start with '/'. Everything under it goes. |

**Returns:** `{ path: string, already_absent: bool, deleted: bool }`

## `duplicate_actor`

*Additive.*

Copy one editor-world actor in place through the editor's duplicate path, keeping its component overrides, and return both the new actor's JSON and the original's. Undoable; it changes the editor SELECTION as a side effect. Matches the INTERNAL name only (no editor labels). The clone exists in memory until save_level writes the .umap -- and a save that answers success while `git status` stays clean means the .umap is read-only (e.g. a Git LFS `lockable` file you have not locked), not that the duplicate failed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Actor's internal name (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Editor labels are NOT accepted; resolve one with find_actors_by_name first. |

**Returns:** `{ duplicated_actor: actor JSON (its auto-assigned name lives here), original_actor: actor JSON }`

## `end_transaction`

*Destructive.*

Close the transaction opened by begin_transaction and COMMIT it, so everything done inside becomes one entry on the editor's undo stack (undo_count grows by one). Pair it with every begin_transaction -- leaving one open makes later edits silently join it. Use cancel_transaction instead when you want the batch thrown away rather than kept.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ success: bool, transaction_index: int (the one that was closed), undo_count: int after the commit }`

## `execute_console_command`

*Destructive.*

Run a console command through the EDITOR (GEditor->Exec against the editor world): cvars, `stat` overlays, `r.*` toggles, engine commands. WARNING: it does NOT reach a running PIE session's PlayerController, so player cheats like `BugItGo` come back handled:false -- to move or cheat a PIE pawn use execute_python against the anchored PIE world. `handled` is the engine's own "some Exec claimed this string", not proof of an effect: verify with the state (get_cvar, a property read), never with this bool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | yes | Console command line, e.g. 'stat fps', 'r.ScreenPercentage 50', 'ShowFlag.Grid 0'. Editor-side only. |

**Returns:** `{ command: string, handled: bool (an Exec handler claimed the string -- not evidence the effect happened) }`

## `execute_python`

*Destructive, open world.*

Execute Python code inside the running Unreal Editor. DO NOT GUESS A FIELD NAME: most of this tool's errors are "object has no attribute" -- and the field usually EXISTS, just not where you reached for it: `HitResult().impact_point` raises, `get_editor_property` cannot find it, and only `to_dict()` returns it (Transform.translation is the reverse). The engine's own stub and Epic's web docs list it either way, so neither settles it -- ask the object (dir(x), x.to_dict(), x.get_editor_property(...)). PIE TRAP -- this tool is the ONE HOLE in the plugin's PIE guard: the commands that compile a Blueprint or write to disk are REFUSED while Play-in-Editor is live (McpPieSafety.gen.h), but arbitrary Python cannot be classified statically, so a script that reaches compile/save through unreal.* (BlueprintEditorLibrary.compile_blueprint, EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset, save_loaded_asset, anything that dirties a Blueprint) RUNS ANYWAY. With PIE live that ends either in a DEAD EDITOR -- the compiler's UREINST_* trampoline retains a world and CheckForWorldGCLeaks is Fatal, taking every unsaved edit with it -- or in a save that reports success without writing a byte (Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0). So: call is_play_in_editor_active FIRST whenever your script compiles, saves, or mutates a Blueprint, and stop PIE before running it. READING the live world during PIE is safe and is exactly what this tool is for -- do not avoid it for that. BEFORE writing a loop, check what already answers it in ONE call: scripts that re-implement something a tool already does fail far more often than scripts doing something genuinely new -- hand-rolled scaffolding is where the errors are, and a bug in the scaffold reads exactly like a finding about the game. enumerate actors of a class -> get_actors_by_class. enumerate them AND read their properties, filtered by class or editor label, drilling into one component, with the answering world STAMPED on the result (this tool cannot tell you which world answered) -> get_actor_properties_by_class. read properties off ONE known object -> get_properties. list an actor's components -> get_actor_components. one line trace -> raycast_scene. sample a property across a whole PIE session ARMED BEFORE BeginPlay -- a window a post-tick callback cannot reach at all -> watch_pie_property. But do NOT read this as "always prefer the specific tool": only a minority of scripts are replaceable end-to-end. Python remains the right answer when the script does what those cannot: several classes in one round trip, walking components AND calling a method, filtering by name substring, correlating two values in the same tick, or anything that mutates. Do not trade one call for twelve. WARNING: `log_output` IS NOT THE LOG OF THE CALL -- it is Python's own prints only (UE fills it from a delegate broadcast solely by unreal.log/log_warning/log_error), so every UE_LOG the ENGINE emits during your script is absent from it. Read `engine_log` instead: it is the GLog slice bracketed to this call, Warning+Error by default. Example: build_meta_human can run, return None, write zero assets and report a clean `log_output` while "LogMetaHumanCoreTechLib: Error: Texture Synthesis has not been initialized" sits in GLog. When a call reports success and NOTHING HAPPENED, `engine_log` is the first place to look; widen with engine_log_level=Log, or pass `log_cursor_before` to get_output_log_lines(since_sequence_id=...) for the unfiltered rest.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | yes | Python code to run (single or multi-line). |
| `capture_output` | boolean | no | Run as a file and collect captured log (default true) |
| `mode` | string | no | Execution mode: ExecuteFile, ExecuteStatement, or EvaluateStatement (default ExecuteFile) |
| `engine_log_level` | string | no | Minimum severity of ENGINE log to return in `engine_log`: Error, Warning (default), Display, Log/All. |
| `engine_log_max` | string | no | Max lines in `engine_log` (default 50, 0 disables, hard cap 4096). |

**Returns:** `{ command, python_success, execution_mode, command_result, output, log_output, log_line_count, engine_log, engine_log_count, engine_log_truncated, log_cursor_before }`

## `execute_python_file`

*Destructive, open world.*

Execute a Python (.py) file inside the running Unreal Editor. PIE TRAP: same hole as execute_python -- arbitrary Python is NOT covered by the plugin's PIE guard, so a script that compiles a Blueprint or saves an asset runs even with Play-in-Editor live, where compiling can KILL the editor (UREINST_* retains a world, CheckForWorldGCLeaks is Fatal) and saving reports success without writing (Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0). Check is_play_in_editor_active first when the file compiles, saves or mutates a Blueprint; reading the live world during PIE is safe. WARNING: `log_output` IS NOT THE LOG OF THE CALL -- it is Python's own prints only (UE fills it from a delegate broadcast solely by unreal.log/log_warning/log_error), so every UE_LOG the ENGINE emits during your script is absent from it. Read `engine_log` instead: it is the GLog slice bracketed to this call, Warning+Error by default. Example: build_meta_human can run, return None, write zero assets and report a clean `log_output` while "LogMetaHumanCoreTechLib: Error: Texture Synthesis has not been initialized" sits in GLog. When a call reports success and NOTHING HAPPENED, `engine_log` is the first place to look; widen with engine_log_level=Log, or pass `log_cursor_before` to get_output_log_lines(since_sequence_id=...) for the unfiltered rest.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file_path` | string | yes | Absolute path to a .py file accessible from the editor host. |
| `engine_log_level` | string | no | Minimum severity of ENGINE log to return in `engine_log`: Error, Warning (default), Display, Log/All. |
| `engine_log_max` | string | no | Max lines in `engine_log` (default 50, 0 disables, hard cap 4096). |

**Returns:** `{ file_path, python_success, command_result, output, log_output, log_line_count, engine_log, engine_log_count, engine_log_truncated, log_cursor_before }`

## `export_assets`

*Destructive.*

Export assets to files via IAssetTools::ExportAssets (preferred format, FBX/PNG/EXR first), each written to export_path/&lt;package path without its leading slash>.&lt;extension>, e.g. D:/Exports/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock.FBX. What was written is measured per asset on disk: exported lists each asset with its file, and not_exported the ones that did not load, have no exporter or failed to write. Succeeds only when every requested asset was written.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_paths` | array | yes | Asset object or package paths to export (e.g. ["/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock"]); empty strings are ignored. |
| `export_path` | string | yes | Destination directory on disk (e.g. "D:/Exports"), created if missing; each file lands in subfolders named after its package path. |

**Returns:** `{ exported_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, export_path: string, exported: [{ asset_path: string, file: string }], not_exported: [string] }`

## `find_actors_by_name`

*Read-only.*

Locate actors by a SUBSTRING of their internal name and/or their editor label, returning name, label, class and transform for each hit. This is the one to use when you know what a thing is CALLED but not its class -- get_actors_by_class needs an exact class name, and this one alone can search labels (match='label'), which is where hand-assigned names live. Plain case-INSENSITIVE substring, no wildcards and no regex: 'turret' matches BP_Turret_C_2, and '*' matches literally nothing. Its world selector is the canonical one: 'editor' (default), 'pie'/'game', 'server', 'client' and 'pie:N' all resolve for real, an unrecognised value FAILS instead of falling through to the editor world, and the reply stamps world_package/world_type/net_mode/pie_instance so you can tell which world answered.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | string | yes | Substring to look for, case-insensitive, no wildcards or regex. Cannot be empty. |
| `match` | string | no | Optional 'name' \| 'label' \| 'both' (default 'both'). 'name' = internal object name only; 'label' = the editor label from the outliner; 'both' = a hit on either. An unknown value is a clean error. |
| `max_results` | number | no | Optional cap on hits (default 1000); results_truncated says whether the scan stopped early. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'game' (alias of 'pie') \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority, GetNetMode() != NM_Client) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' (the PIE context whose PIEInstance is N). Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world. |

**Returns:** `{ matching_actors: [ { name, actor_name, label, class, location, rotation, scale, is_loaded } ], matching_actors_count: int, search_pattern: string, match: string, results_truncated: bool, max_results: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (in World Partition the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }`

## `find_duplicate_assets`

*Read-only.*

Find groups of assets sharing the same base name under a folder tree (e.g. same name existing under both a vendored library tree and a first-party fork)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `folder_path` | string | no | Content folder to scan, default /Game |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | If true, scan subfolders, default true |
| `min_group_size` | number | no | Minimum number of same-named assets to report as a duplicate group, default 2 |
| `class_filter` | array | no | Optional list of class short names (e.g. "StaticMesh","Material"); only assets whose AssetClassPath short name case-insensitively matches one of these are considered |
| `max_results` | number | no | Cap on the number of duplicate GROUPS returned (not raw assets), clamped 1..20000, default 2000 |

**Returns:** `{ folder_path, recursive, class_filter, min_group_size, group_count, total_duplicate_assets, assets_scanned, max_results, results_truncated, groups: [{ name, count, classes: [string], assets: [{path, package, class}] }] } (groups sorted by count descending)`

## `find_unused_assets`

*Read-only.*

Find assets in a folder with zero referencers, and annotate each survivor with the reasons it should be KEPT anyway. "Zero referencers" is not the same as "safe to delete": there are three common ways an asset stays alive with an empty referencer set -- it is explicitly protected, a Config/Default*.ini names it, or it is a fork descending from a vendored base library. Each becomes a keep_reason string on the entry; deletion_candidates lists only the entries with NO keep_reason. Nothing is ever removed from unused_assets by these flags (hiding a genuinely unreferenced asset would be the same lie in the other direction). NOTE: there is deliberately no `is_world` -- it is already visible in class_name ("World").

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `folder_path` | string | yes | Content folder to scan, e.g. /Game/Unused |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | If true, scan subfolders, default true |
| `exclude_classes` | array | no | Optional list of class name fragments to skip |
| `dependency_type` | string | no | Referencer filter: "hard"\|"soft"\|"all" (case-insensitive), default "all" (identical behavior to omitting it) |
| `protect_paths` | array | no | Wildcard patterns (FString::MatchesWildcard, case-insensitive, `*` spans '/') matched against the package name and the object path. Default [] . A match adds keep_reason "protected_path". |
| `include_lineage_reasons` | boolean | no | Default FALSE because it LOADS every candidate Blueprint. When true, a Blueprint whose super chain reaches a class owned by one of base_libraries gets keep_reason "descends_from_base_library" -- the only signal that saves a fork carrying no fork-origin tag (project setting Fork Origin Tag). |
| `base_libraries` | array | no | Vendored-library content roots for the lineage check. Default: the project's Read Only Content Roots (same default as audit_class_purity). |

**Returns:** `{ folder_path, folder_exists, recursive, dependency_type, protect_paths: [string], include_lineage_reasons, base_libraries: [string], unused_assets: [{path, class_name, size_kb, keep_reasons: [string], keep_reason_detail: {...}}], unused_count, total_scanned, deletion_candidates: [string], deletion_candidate_count, assets_with_keep_reason, keep_reason_counts: {protected_path, referenced_by_config, descends_from_base_library}, config_scan: {files_scanned: int, files: [string]}, lineage_scan: {attempted, blueprints_loaded, skipped_non_blueprint, load_failures} }`

## `fixup_redirectors`

*Destructive.*

Clean up the redirectors a rename/move left behind, under a folder: load each referencing package (which repoints it) and re-save it, optionally force-deleting redirectors whose referencers all saved. Hand-rolled on purpose -- IAssetTools::FixupReferencers HARD-CRASHES on World-Partition/OFPA projects -- and heavily railed: it REFUSES while PIE is active, never writes under readonly_roots (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots), never outside /Game, and never loads or saves map or OFPA packages, handing the resident ones back in skipped_current_world for you to save_level instead. Deletions are DISK-verified (a redirector whose .uasset survives lands in redirectors_delete_failed, not in the count). WARNING: redirectors_found/deleted count OBJECTS: one renamed Blueprint leaves THREE in a single package -- read redirector_packages_found for files.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | no | Long path to scan, defaults to /Game |
| `delete_redirectors` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false). After a successful repoint, force-delete the redirectors whose every non-redirector referencer was saved. Left in place by default (a redirector is ~2 KB and harmless). |
| `readonly_roots` | array | no | Optional array of long-path prefixes that must NEVER be written (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots, i.e. the vendored library roots). Referencers under them are reported in skipped_readonly instead of being saved. |

**Returns:** `{ path: string, redirectors_found: int, redirector_packages_found: int, referencers_repointed: int, packages_saved: int, packages_failed: [{ package: string, error: string }], skipped_readonly: [string], skipped_current_world: [string], redirectors_deleted: int, redirector_packages_deleted: int, redirectors_delete_failed: [{ package: string, reason: string }], redirectors_fixed: int, message: string }`

## `get_actors_in_level`

*Read-only.*

Dump EVERY actor of a world (name, class, transform), capped by max_results at 5000, with total_actors_in_level and results_truncated so you know if you saw all of it. The unfiltered census: reach for get_actors_by_class when you know the class, find_actors_by_name for a name/label substring, get_actors_in_radius for a place. Its world selector is the canonical one: 'editor' (default), 'pie'/'game', 'server', 'client' and 'pie:N' all resolve for real, an unrecognised value FAILS naming the worlds that exist instead of quietly answering from the editor world, and every reply carries world_package/world_type/net_mode/pie_instance so you can see WHICH world answered rather than assuming.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_results` | number | no | Optional cap on returned actors (default 5000). Must be > 0. Truncation is reported, never silent. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'game' (alias of 'pie') \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority, GetNetMode() != NM_Client) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' (the PIE context whose PIEInstance is N). Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world. |

**Returns:** `{ actors: [actor JSON], actors_count: int, total_actors_in_level: int, results_truncated: bool, max_results: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (in World Partition the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }`

## `get_automation_test_results`

*Read-only.*

Returns the cached result of the last synchronous test completed through run_automation_test, without running anything: test_name, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings and entries. Skipped or multi-tick tests leave the cache unchanged; fails when no test has completed this editor session.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ test_name, started, completed, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings, entries:[{type,message,context,filename,line}], entry_count }`

## `get_current_level`

*Read-only.*

Which map a world is sitting on: level_name, its package_name (/Game/... or /Engine/...), the resolved disk filename, whether the package is dirty, and a live actor count. package_name is the discriminator that catches the classic mistake -- if it starts with /Engine/ you are on an engine template (what load_level with default_template=true leaves behind) and a save_level without `filename` would overwrite the ENGINE's own map. Defaults to the EDITOR world; it also takes the standard `world` selector, so during PIE you can ask the play world ('pie'/'server'/'client'/'pie:N') instead of being told about the authoring map and having no way to know it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default -- the authoring map even while PIE runs) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'game' (alias of 'pie') \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N'. Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent fallback to the editor world. |

**Returns:** `{ level_name: string, package_name: string (the /Game or /Engine path -- read this one), filename: string, is_dirty: bool, actor_count: int, world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE, not in world_name), world_type: string ("Editor" | "PIE" | ...), net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }`

## `get_cvar`

*Read-only.*

Reads a console variable's live value, help text, and flags.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Console variable name, e.g. "r.ScreenPercentage". |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, value: string, string_value: string, int_value: int, float_value: float, bool_value: bool, help: string, flags: int, set_by: string }`

## `get_engine_ini_value`

*Read-only.*

Read one key from the merged in-memory config (GConfig) of an INI such as Engine or Game. Read-only; returns value and found (false, with an empty value, when the section or key is missing). Pass config_file without .ini. Writer: set_engine_ini_value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `section` | string | yes | Section name (e.g. "/Script/Engine.RendererSettings") |
| `key` | string | yes | Key inside the section, e.g. "r.DefaultFeature.AntiAliasing". |
| `config_file` | string | no | Config base name without extension, e.g. "Engine" (default), "Game", "Input", "Editor", "Scalability"; "Engine.ini" is not resolved. |

## `get_level_blueprint`

*Additive.*

Get (or, with create=true, bring into being) the current level's Level Blueprint and return the blueprint_path that the graph tools need -- its event graph is always called "EventGraph", so add_graph_node / connect_pins can target it directly with graph_name="EventGraph". This is the entry point for level-specific scripting that does not belong in any actor. Read-only by default: with create=false and no blueprint present it answers exists:false + success:true rather than failing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false). True creates the Level Blueprint if the level has none -- a mutation that dirties the map, so save_level afterwards. |

**Returns:** `{ exists: true, created: bool, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_name: string, event_graph: "EventGraph", level_name: string, success: true }, or, when no blueprint exists and create=false: { exists: false, success: true, level_name: string, note: string }`

## `get_media_info`

*Read-only.*

Read a media asset by path: class and media_type ("MediaPlayer", "MediaTexture", "FileMediaSource" or "Other"), plus play_on_open and loop for a player, the linked player and auto_clear for a texture, or file_path for a file source. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Path of a UMediaPlayer, UMediaTexture or UFileMediaSource asset, e.g. "/Game/Media/MP_Intro"; any other asset reports only its name and class. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, asset_name, class, media_type, play_on_open, loop, has_media_player, media_player_path, auto_clear, file_path }`

## `get_message_log_entries`

*Read-only.*

Read back the messages currently in a named engine Message Log listing (IMessageLogListing::GetFilteredMessages), each resolved back to the actor/component the engine attached to it. The reader that pairs with add_message_log_entry/clear_message_log.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log_name` | string | yes | The message log listing name (e.g. "PIE", "MapCheck", or a custom name). Required. |
| `severity` | string | no | Optional severity filter: "Error"\|"PerformanceWarning"\|"Warning"\|"Info" (case-insensitive). Omit for all. |
| `base_libraries` | array | no | Package roots to classify each entry's class against (optional, default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). An explicit [] disables the classification. Reported as data in class_root/class_root_is_base_library; the tool never judges which root is "upstream". |

**Returns:** `{ log_name: string, severity_filter: string|null, base_libraries: [string], entries: [{message: string, severity: string, token_source: string, object_path: string, object_resolved: bool, actor_name: string, actor_label: string, actor_path: string, actor_class: string, actor_guid: string, component_name: string, class_asset_path: string, class_root: string, class_root_is_base_library: bool}], count: int }`

## `get_output_log_lines`

*Read-only.*

Read the single per-editor-session log buffer UEAgent attaches to GLog (general editor output, not PIE-only -- Serialize() captures every category/verbosity that passes through GLog, regardless of PIE state; usable for PIE Functional Test / wait_for_pie_completion orchestration too). NON-DESTRUCTIVE cursor read (since_sequence_id, same idiom as poll_gameplay_messages), structured entries. Supports all three filters (message text, verbosity level, category).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | number | no | Optional int32 cap on the number of entries returned (default 200, max 4096). |
| `filter` | string | no | Optional case-insensitive substring on the message text. |
| `level_filter` | string | no | Optional exact verbosity name filter (Fatal\|Error\|Warning\|Display\|Log\|Verbose\|VeryVerbose), case-insensitive. |
| `category_filter` | string | no | Optional case-insensitive substring on the log category name. |
| `since_sequence_id` | number | no | Optional int64 cursor; only entries with a higher sequence_id are returned (default 0 = everything currently retained). |

**Returns:** `{ lines: [{sequence_id, ts, level, category, message}], count, held_total, last_sequence_id }`

Reports whether the editor Python plugin is loaded, available, configured and initialized, with the interpreter path and engine version; when Python is initialized it also evaluates sys.version for python_version (empty otherwise). Changes nothing; check it before execute_python or execute_python_file.

No parameters.

## `get_selected_actors`

*Read-only.*

Read what is selected in the editor viewport/outliner right now: each actor's JSON plus the count and the world it belongs to. Use it to act on "what the user just clicked" without asking for names, and as the read-back for select_actors / deselect_actors. Editor world only, and remember that delete_actor, duplicate_actor, copy_actors and move_actors_to_level all MUTATE the selection as a side effect -- read it before those, not after.

No parameters.

## `get_struct_members`

*Read-only.*

List the members of a user-defined struct (UUserDefinedStruct) with their type, default value, and flags.  The reader that pairs with add_struct_member.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `struct_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedStruct (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyStruct). |

## `get_transaction_history`

*Read-only.*

Read the editor's undo buffer as a list, most-recent-first: each entry's title, context, primary object and whether it has already been undone. Use it to answer "what changed the editor recently, and was it me" -- including edits made by the human in the UI -- before you undo anything or blame a tool for a state you did not expect. Pure read; get_undo_state gives the counts-only summary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_entries` | number | no | Max entries to return, newest first (default 50, clamped to 1..500). |

**Returns:** `{ count: int, entries: [{ queue_index: int, title: string, context: string, is_transient: bool, primary_object: string, is_undone: bool }] }`

## `get_undo_state`

*Read-only.*

One call that answers everything you need before touching undo/redo: both counts, both next-entry LABELS, why undo or redo is impossible right now, and whether a transaction is still OPEN (transaction_open -- the thing that silently swallows later edits into someone else's batch). Read it BEFORE undo so you know what you are about to revert.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ can_undo: bool, can_redo: bool, undo_reason?: string (why not, when can_undo is false), redo_reason?: string (why not, when can_redo is false), undo_count: int (entries undo can still revert), redo_count: int (undone entries redo can restore), next_undo: string, next_redo: string, transaction_open: bool, transaction_index: int }`

## `get_viewport_state`

*Read-only.*

Read the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first) without changing it: realtime (the effective value, an override such as the background throttle included), view mode name and index, camera speed, camera location [x, y, z] and rotation [pitch, yaw, roll], and the Grid, Bounds, Collision, Wireframe and Lighting show flags, a flag this engine lacks left out. view_mode names every engine view mode by its display name without spaces (Lit, CSGWireframe, PlayerCollision...), or ViewMode_&lt;index> for a value the engine does not name; set_viewport_view_mode takes that name back, but refuses the modes that need a choice made with them. It also reads the perspective FOV, the near clip plane and far clip override, the exposure, the view type (perspective or an orthographic view) and whether cinematic tools may possess the viewport. No viewport is an error; nothing is saved or recorded for undo. Setters: set_viewport_view_mode, set_viewport_realtime, set_camera_speed, set_viewport_camera, set_show_flag, set_viewport_fov, set_near_clip_plane, set_far_clip_plane, set_viewport_exposure, set_view_type, set_allow_cinematic_control.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ realtime: bool, view_mode_index: int, view_mode: string, camera_speed: number, location: [number], rotation: [number], show_flags: object, fov: number (current perspective FOV, degrees), near_clip_plane: number (effective, cm), far_clip_plane_override: number (< 0 when no override is engaged), exposure: { fixed: bool, ev100: number }, view_type: string, view_type_index: int, allows_cinematic_control: bool }`

## `import_font_file`

*Destructive.*

Import a .ttf/.otf/.ttc/.otc font from disk as a UFontFace, and optionally the companion UFont that a FSlateFontInfo needs to actually render text. This is the only way to get a typeface into the project headlessly: import_texture_file imports images only, and nothing else in the toolset touches fonts. Drives UFontFileImportFactory inline (never IAssetTools::ImportAssets, which asserts when re-entered from the engine tick) and ALWAYS sets BatchCreateFontAsset explicitly -- left at its default the factory pops a MODAL DIALOG asking whether to create the UFont, which would hang the editor on a click that is never coming. Once imported, point a widget at it with set_widget_property on the dotted path "Font.FontObject" (a UFont) plus "Font.TypefaceFontName", or "Font.Size" for the size.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_file_path` | string | yes | Absolute path on disk to the .ttf/.otf/.ttc/.otc file. A missing file, or any other extension, is a clean error before anything is touched. |
| `destination_path` | string | yes | UE long path of the destination content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame/UI/Fonts. |
| `name` | string | no | Optional asset name; defaults to the source file's base name. |
| `create_font_asset` | boolean | no | Also create the companion UFont asset (default true). A UFontFace alone is a raw typeface: a FSlateFontInfo's FontObject wants a UFont. Pass false to import only the face, e.g. to add it as another typeface entry of an existing font. |

**Returns:** `{ source_file_path, destination_path, imported_object_path, font_face_created, create_font_asset, message }`

## `link_media_texture_to_player`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind a UMediaTexture asset to a UMediaPlayer asset (both by asset path) so the texture shows that player's video, in place of any player it was bound to, in one undo step; then save the texture package (the player asset is not modified). The link is written to the texture's saved MediaPlayer property, so it survives a reload; linked confirms both that property and the player the texture now reports (bound_player_path), and a link that did not take is an error with linked false and nothing saved. Idempotent: linking the same pair again writes and saves the same state. A missing texture or player is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Create the assets with create_media_texture and create_media_player (which can also make a linked texture); read back with get_media_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `media_texture_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UMediaTexture, e.g. "/Game/Media/T_Intro" (the object path form also works). |
| `media_player_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UMediaPlayer to bind, e.g. "/Game/Media/MP_Intro" (the object path form also works). |

**Returns:** `{ media_texture_path, media_player_path, linked, saved, bound_player_path?, save_error? }`

List registered automation tests in the editor (read-only; does not run them)

| `filter` | string | no | Optional case-insensitive substring matched against the full test path |
| `max_results` | number | no | Cap on returned entries (default 500) |

## `list_cvars`

*Read-only.*

Lists registered console variables whose name contains a substring, or starts with prefix.  Iterates IConsoleManager::Get().ForEachConsoleObjectThatContains(filter) (ForEachConsoleObjectThatStartsWith(prefix) when prefix is given), collecting only console *variables* unless include_commands also lists console commands, capped at max_results. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string | no | Substring filter for cvar names (empty matches all); with prefix, a name must match both. |
| `prefix` | string | no | Optional name prefix, case-insensitive, e.g. "r.Shadow." or "t."; when given only names starting with it are listed. |
| `include_commands` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false): also list console commands, entries with a name and help but no value. |

## `list_dirty_packages`

*Read-only.*

What is UNSAVED in the editor right now: every dirty package with its disk path, split into map / OFPA-external / asset, and -- the reason to run it -- readonly_dirty_count, the single go/no-go number telling you a vendored root like /Game/VendorPack would be REWRITTEN by the next bulk save. Run it before closing the editor, before compiling, and before any save; it also resolves OFPA hashes to actor labels so /__ExternalActors__/AB/CD/EF12 becomes a name. Strictly read-only: never marks dirty, never saves. WARNING: it reports IN-MEMORY state only -- a package clean here can still differ from HEAD on disk, so `git status` stays the disk authority. And do NOT use its pie_active field as the PIE gate: it can answer false with PIE running; the oracle is is_play_in_editor_active.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `readonly_roots` | array | no | Optional array of long-path prefixes treated as vendored/upstream (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). Only used to CLASSIFY (under_readonly_root / readonly_dirty_count); nothing is ever written. Pass [] to switch the classification off. |
| `path_prefix` | string | no | Optional long-path prefix filter, e.g. /Game/VendorPack, to ask "is anything of THEIRS dirty". Empty (default) lists everything; what it excluded is counted in filtered_out. |
| `include_objects` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false). Also list every object carried by each dirty package. One object-hash walk per package -- a dirty map can hold thousands, so leave it off unless you need the contents. |

**Returns:** `{ dirty_count: int, readonly_dirty_count: int, map_dirty_count: int, external_dirty_count: int, asset_dirty_count: int, filtered_out: int, pie_active: bool, current_world_package: string, path_prefix: string, readonly_roots: [string], readonly_roots_defaulted: bool, packages: [{ package_name: string, file_path: string, exists_on_disk: bool, kind: string, contains_map: bool, newly_created: bool, actor_label: string, actor_name: string, asset_name: string, asset_class: string, under_readonly_root: bool, objects?: [string] }], message: string, note: string }`

## `list_engine_ini_sections`

*Read-only.*

List the section names of one INI in the merged in-memory config (GConfig), like get_engine_ini_value reads it: count, sections, found (false when GConfig does not know that INI) and file_path. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config_file` | string | no | INI base name, e.g. "Engine" (default), "Game", "Input", "Editor", "Scalability"; a trailing ".ini" is dropped. |
| `include_base` | boolean | no | Ignored: the code reads it but never uses it, so Base.ini sections are neither added nor removed. |

**Returns:** `{ count, sections: [string], found: bool, config_file, file_path }`

## `load_level`

*Destructive.*

Open a map in the editor (by /Game or /Engine package path, or disk .umap), replacing the current world; default_template=true opens the engine's default template level instead (/Engine/Maps/Templates/Template_Default, ~45 actors: floor, PlayerStart, sky and lights), after which a save_level without `filename` would write over the ENGINE's own map (is_engine_template and warning say so). Also the repair for actors that VANISHED from a world in memory after compile_blueprint: reloading the same map brings the placed OFPA instances back with their per-instance config -- never re-place them. REFUSES up front when any other UWorld is still resident in memory, because the engine's world-leak check turns that into a Fatal error that kills the editor process and every unsaved edit with it; the refusal lists the resident worlds and the remedy. Run list_dirty_packages first: a reload discards unsaved work.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filename` | string | no | Disk path to a .umap, OR a long package path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Foo) resolved to the on-disk map file. Required unless default_template is true. |
| `default_template` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false): open the engine's default template level (/Engine/Maps/Templates/Template_Default) without naming it in filename; giving both is an error. |
| `load_as_template` | boolean | no | When true, loads the level as a template; defaults to false |
| `force` | boolean | no | Skip the resident-world preflight and call LoadMap anyway. With resident worlds alive this PROBABLY KILLS THE EDITOR: the engine raises a Fatal error ("World Memory Leaks"), the process dies and every unsaved in-memory edit is lost. Defaults to false. |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool, error?: string, refused?: bool, load_attempted?: bool, resident_world_count?: int, resident_worlds?: [{ package: string, world_name: string, world_type: string, has_world_context: bool, is_load_target: bool }], remedy?: string, data?: { loaded_filename: string, target_package: string, default_template: bool, level_name?: string, world_name?: string, loaded_package?: string, is_engine_template?: bool, warning?: string (when the loaded map belongs to the engine), resident_world_count: int, forced_past_resident_worlds: bool, resident_worlds?: [...] } }`

## `migrate_assets`

*Destructive.*

Copy assets, and their dependencies unless ignore_dependencies, into another project's Content folder with IAssetTools::MigratePackages, with no prompt and skipping files that already exist there. The engine first saves every dirty package of this editor, and migrates nothing if one of them fails to save. What was copied is measured from the migration's own package list against the disk: migrated lists each package written (dependencies included), skipped_existing the requested ones the destination already had, failed the requested ones neither written nor skipped. Succeeds when nothing requested failed. destination_path must be a Content folder with a .uproject (or one .uplugin) next to it, or the engine migrates nothing and the call fails.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_paths` | array | yes | Asset object or package paths to migrate (e.g. ["/Game/Props/SM_Crate"]); each is reduced to its package name. |
| `destination_path` | string | yes | Target content folder, e.g. D:/OtherProject/Content |
| `ignore_dependencies` | boolean | no | When true only the listed packages are copied, without their dependencies (default false). |

**Returns:** `{ migrated_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, destination_path: string, ignore_dependencies: bool, migrated: [{ package: string, file: string }], skipped_existing: [string], failed: [string], note: string? }`

## `move_actors_to_level`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Relocate existing editor-world actors into another sub-level (persistent or a loaded streaming level) -- it rescues actors that got spawned into the wrong level, which set_current_level only prevents going forward. Idempotent: actors already there come back in already_in_level instead of being touched. WARNING: it is clipboard-backed, so the editor SELECTION is mutated as a side effect, and the destination must be loaded AND unlocked. Both levels' packages get dirty: save_level after.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_names` | array | yes | Array of actor names OR editor labels in the editor world (this one does accept labels, unlike delete_actor/delete_actors). |
| `target_level` | string | yes | "persistent" or the short name of a loaded streaming sub-level |
| `move_all_or_fail` | boolean | no | When true, fail the whole move if any actor cannot be moved; defaults to false |

**Returns:** `{ requested: int, moved_count: int, already_in_level: [string], target_level: string, success: bool, note: string }`

## `open_message_log`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Open or focus the editor Message Log window on one listing (PIE by default), creating the listing empty when it does not exist yet and enabling message log display; no message is changed. opened only says the request was made: without an editor UI nothing shows. module_available says whether the MessageLog module loaded. To read the messages use get_message_log_entries rather than the window; add or empty them with add_message_log_entry and clear_message_log.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log_name` | string | no | Listing to surface (default "PIE"). |

**Returns:** `{ opened: bool, log_name: string, module_available: bool }`

## `paste_actors`

*Destructive.*

Drop whatever copy_actors left on the editor clipboard into the current level (edactPasteSelected), optionally re-centring the whole group on a world location while KEEPING each actor's relative offset -- that is the point of the copy/paste pair versus duplicate_actor. The pasted actors end up selected and are returned with their new names and transforms. Editor world only; they live in memory until save_level writes the .umap.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `location` | array | no | Optional world point to centre the pasted group on, ARRAY form only [x, y, z] (the group's average is moved there, each actor's offset preserved). Omit to paste where the originals were; any other value (an object, another length) is an error and nothing is pasted. |

**Returns:** `{ pasted_actors: [actor JSON with the new auto-assigned names], pasted_count: int, success: bool }`

## `place_actor_on_terrain`

*Additive.*

Ground an actor on the landscape by sampling the heightmap at its XY (no line trace; traces miss the landscape headless). Sets the actor's Z so either its mesh bbox bottom or its origin sits at the sampled height + z_offset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Internal name of the actor to place (Actor->GetName()) |
| `align` | string | no | Optional 'mesh_bbox_bottom' (default; drops the lowest mesh-geometry point onto the ground) or 'actor_origin' (puts the actor origin at the ground) |
| `z_offset` | number | no | Optional extra world-Z added above the sampled ground height; defaults to 0 |

**Returns:** `{ actor: actor JSON, landed_z: number (sampled ground world-Z), previous_z: number, new_z: number, sampled_from: 'heightmap', in_bounds: bool, align: string, align_used: string, z_offset: number, landscape_actor_name: string }`

## `place_actors_on_terrain`

*Additive.*

Ground many actors on the landscape in one call by sampling the heightmap at each actor's XY (no line trace; scatter without per-point python). Same grounding math as place_actor_on_terrain, applied per actor.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actors` | array | yes | Array of { name (Actor->GetName()) OR label (Actor->GetActorLabel()), z_offset? (per-actor override), align? ('mesh_bbox_bottom'\|'actor_origin', per-actor override) } |
| `align` | string | no | Optional default align for entries without their own; 'mesh_bbox_bottom' (default; drops the lowest mesh point) or 'actor_origin' |
| `z_offset` | number | no | Optional default extra world-Z above the sampled ground for entries without their own; defaults to 0 |

**Returns:** `{ placed: [ { name, label, previous_z, new_z, landed_z, in_bounds, align, align_used, z_offset } ], failed: [ { name?, label?, error } ], placed_count: int, failed_count: int, requested_count: int, landscape_actor_name: string, world_name: string }`

## `print_to_output_log`

*Additive.*

Write one line to the editor Output Log under the LogTemp category, at Log, Warning or Error verbosity; verbosity is matched without case, anything else logs at Log, and the reply's verbosity is the level actually used. An empty or missing message is an error. Each call appends another line, so it is not idempotent, and nothing else changes: no asset, no undo step, no Message Log entry; like any UE_LOG line it also reaches the editor log file. Use it to mark a point in the log between other calls; read lines back with get_output_log_lines; a listing in Window > Message Log is add_message_log_entry, an on-screen toast show_notification.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | yes | The text to log; empty is an error. |
| `verbosity` | string | no | UE_LOG verbosity: "Log" (default), "Warning", "Error"; matched without case, and any other value logs at Log. |

**Returns:** `{ logged: bool, message: string, verbosity: string }`

## `redo`

*Destructive.*

Re-apply the transaction that undo just reverted, or `count` of them, and report what remains, including next_redo. WARNING: `success` is ALWAYS true even with an empty redo stack -- read `applied` instead, and with a count compare actually_redone against requested. Note the redo stack is discarded as soon as any NEW edit is made after an undo, so a redo that answers applied:false usually means something was changed in between, not that the command failed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | number | no | Optional. How many transactions to redo, at least 1 (default 1); stops early when the redo stack runs out. Below 1 is refused. |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool (THE oracle), requested: int, actually_redone: int (compare against requested), undo_count: int, can_redo: bool, next_redo: string (label of the next redoable entry) }`

## `reload_asset_package`

*Destructive.*

Re-read already-loaded packages FROM DISK, non-interactively (it never opens the modal that would freeze a headless editor), either preserving or permanently discarding their in-memory edits. This is the repair for the situation list_dirty_packages flags: a vendored package left dirty by a compile cascade is cleaned with on_dirty="discard" (was_dirty:[...] -> still_dirty:[]), so the next bulk save cannot write it. Also the way to throw away a bad in-memory edit without touching disk. It reports before/after evidence per package, and skips what it cannot safely reload (not loaded, OFPA, worlds) instead of pretending. WARNING: on_dirty="discard" is irreversible for unsaved work -- check what is dirty first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_names` | array | no | Array of long package names (or object paths) to reload, e.g. ["/Game/VendorPack/.../DT_ItemRows"]. |
| `package_name` | string | no | Convenience single-name alias for package_names. |
| `on_dirty` | string | no | Optional "abort" (default) or "discard". "abort" -> EReloadPackagesInteractionMode::AssumeNegative: a package with unsaved in-memory edits is NOT reloaded and its edits are kept. "discard" -> AssumePositive: UPackageTools clears the dirty flag and reloads, PERMANENTLY THROWING AWAY those in-memory edits. |

**Returns:** `{ requested: [string], on_dirty: string, interaction_mode: string, attempted: [string], reloaded: [string], was_dirty: [string], still_dirty: [string], failed: [string], skipped_not_loaded: [string], skipped_ofpa: [string], skipped_world: [object], skipped_invalid: [object], api_returned: bool, api_error: string, verify: { before: [object], after: [object] }, message: string }`

## `remove_component_from_actor`

*Destructive.*

Detach and destroy one component from an actor PLACED in the level, by component name -- the inverse of add_component_to_actor and, like it, an instance-level edit that does not touch the actor's Blueprint (use remove_component_from_blueprint for the class). Discover the exact component_name with get_actor_components first. Editor world only; dirties the actor's package, so save_level to keep it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Name of the placed actor (editor world). |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Exact component name as reported by get_actor_components. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name: string, removed_component: string, component_type: string, success: bool }`

## `remove_enum_entry`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove one enumerator from a Blueprint Enum by display name (or internal name).  Idempotent (a missing entry reports already_absent without error); refuses to remove the last remaining entry. The hidden _MAX sentinel is never counted or removable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum. |
| `entry_name` | string | yes | Enumerator to remove, by display name (or internal name). |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, entry_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, entry_count: int }`

## `remove_struct_member`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a member from a user-defined struct.  Idempotent (a missing member reports already_absent without error); the engine refuses to remove the last remaining member (a struct cannot be empty) -- reported as an honest error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `struct_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedStruct. |
| `member_name` | string | yes | Member to remove, by its display name (or internal var name). |

**Returns:** `{ struct_path: string, member_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, member_count: int }`

## `remove_undo_barrier`

*Destructive.*

Lift the most recent undo barrier so undo can step past it again -- the counterpart of set_undo_barrier, for when the protected batch is finished -- or, with all=true, every barrier at once (including ones another session or the human placed to protect their work). Nothing is undone; it only lifts the floor. WARNING: `success` is hardcoded true: `removed` is the oracle and comes back false as an honest no-op when there was no barrier.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `all` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false). true clears ALL undo barriers instead of popping the most recent one. |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool (hardcoded), removed: bool (THE oracle -- false = there was nothing to pop), all: bool (echo), undo_barrier: int now in force, undo_count: int, queue_length: int }`

## `rename_enum_entry`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rename one enumerator of a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum): resolve the entry by its current display name (or internal name) to its index, then set a new display name via FEnumEditorUtils::SetEnumeratorDisplayName.  Idempotent: renaming an entry to the name it already has is a no-op success (already_named). An unknown current entry is an honest error; so is a new name that is empty/invalid or duplicates another entry's display name (the engine's IsEnumeratorDisplayNameValid rejects it). The hidden _MAX sentinel is never addressable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum). |
| `entry_name` | string | yes | Enumerator to rename, by its current display name (or internal name). |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New display name for the enumerator. |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, entry_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, index: int, entries: [string] }`

## `rename_struct_member`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rename a member of a user-defined struct by resolving its current display name to its stable VarGuid, then applying the new display name (the same FStructureEditorUtils::RenameVariable path add_struct_member uses to set the initial name).  Idempotent: renaming a member to the name it already has is a no-op success (already_named). An unknown current member, or a new name that collides with another member's name, is an honest error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `struct_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedStruct. |
| `member_name` | string | yes | Member to rename, by its current display name (or internal var name). |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New display name for the member. |

**Returns:** `{ struct_path: string, member_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, member: object }`

## `reorder_enum_entry`

*Destructive.*

Move one enumerator to a new position in a Blueprint Enum, shifting the others (e.g. [A,B,C,D] move B->index 2 = [A,C,B,D]).  to_index is clamped to the user-entry range (the trailing _MAX sentinel is excluded). An unknown entry is an honest error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum. |
| `entry_name` | string | yes | Enumerator to move, by display name (or internal name). |
| `to_index` | number | yes | Target zero-based position among the user entries. |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, entry_name: string, from_index: int, to_index: int, moved: bool, entries: [string] }`

## `reset_transaction_buffer`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

IRREVERSIBLE: wipes the editor's ENTIRE undo AND redo history (the human's entries too, not just yours) and drops any open transaction. It does not revert anything -- edits already made stay made, they just stop being undoable. Use only to reclaim memory after a huge batch, or when a corrupt buffer is causing trouble; to undo work use undo (with `count` for several steps). undo_count_before vs after is the evidence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | no | Human-readable reason, logged by the engine so the wipe is traceable. Defaults to 'MCP reset_transaction_buffer'. |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool (hardcoded), undo_count_before: int, undo_count_after: int (0) }`

*Destructive.*

Run a single automation test by name and return its result (synchronous tests only)

| `test_name` | string | yes | The exact registered test name (the "test_name" field from list_automation_tests) |

**Returns:** `{ test_name, started, completed, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings, entries:[{type,message,context,filename,line}], entry_count, note }`

*Destructive.*

Start a Play-in-Editor session that runs the named AFunctionalTest BP and return the test verdict. Requires the named BP to exist; it will be auto-added to the current editor world's "PrepareForPIE" list so PIE picks it up. Honest-gated: returns success=false (not an error) if PIE fails to start -- the harness detects a transport drop separately.

| `test_asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the AFunctionalTest BP asset (e.g. "/Game/Tests/BP_FT_PlayerHealth"). |
| `auto_stop_pie` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). After the test completes (pass/fail), stop PIE and return the verdict. |
