*Destructive.*

Runs every registered automation test with the smoke filter, synchronously in the editor, and returns only the aggregate: ran, all_passed and a note. Under a commandlet the engine skips them, so ran and all_passed come back false. For one test with its log entries use run_automation_test.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ ran, all_passed, note }`

## `save_asset`

*Destructive.*

Write ONE .uasset to disk by package path (a Blueprint, DataTable, material...) and VERIFY the effect: still_dirty_after_save:false plus file_on_disk:true is the oracle, not `saved`. Use save_level for the .umap and reload_asset_package to undo an in-memory edit instead. PIE: this is REFUSED while Play-in-Editor runs (it never stops or touches your session) -- the engine guard Editor.AllowSavingAssetsDuringPIE=0 rejects the write before attempting anything, so a save during play would report success without writing a byte. Stop PIE and retry, or pass force=true. WARNING: when it answers success:false with PIE down, a common cause is the file being READ-ONLY on disk (e.g. a Git LFS `lockable` file that has not been `git lfs lock`ed). You do not have to check that by hand: `file_read_only` is measured on every call and the error message states whether a read-only file IS or is NOT the explanation. WARNING: it writes exactly one package, so it cannot stop a compile cascade from dirtying a vendored asset that a LATER bulk save then rewrites -- list_dirty_packages before, `git status` after.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Full asset path to save, e.g. /Game/MyGame/Core/BP_MyActor (an .Object suffix is tolerated). Must already exist or the call errors. |
| `readonly_roots` | array | no | Optional array of long-path prefixes treated as vendored/upstream (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). A save under one of them is REFUSED by default; see refuse_readonly. Pass [] to disable the classification entirely. |
| `refuse_readonly` | boolean | no | Optional bool. When true, a save whose package falls under one of readonly_roots is REFUSED (success:false, saved:false, refused_readonly:true) instead of performed. Default = the process-wide switch (mcp_common::IsReadOnlyRootSaveEnforcementEnabled(), true unless `mcp.ReadOnlyRootEnforcement 0`); when false the write happens and is only reported + ledgered. |

**Returns:** `` { path: string, package_name: string, saved: bool, success: bool, under_readonly_root: bool, readonly_root_matched: string, refused_readonly: bool, readonly_roots: [string], readonly_roots_defaulted: bool, still_dirty_after_save: bool, file_on_disk: bool, file_read_only: bool (measured on disk -- true means the file is read-only, e.g. an unlocked Git LFS `lockable` file), verification: object, verification_checks: [object], error?: string } ``

## `save_level`

*Destructive.*

Write the editor's current level (.umap) to disk; it REFUSES while PIE is running (the engine guard rejects the write anyway) and derives `success` from the file being on disk afterwards, never from the save call's own bool. WARNING: it also REFUSES when the target .umap is READ-ONLY on disk, which in an LFS repo means a `lockable` path you have not `git lfs lock`ed: that write cannot succeed, and answering over HEAD's still-untouched bytes would report success:true having written nothing. The refusal names the file and the fix (`git lfs lock <file>`) -- take the lock, do not retry. WARNING: on a file that ALREADY existed, `file_exists_on_disk` alone still cannot tell "I wrote it" from "it was already there": the field that proves the write is `file_mtime_changed`. It is deliberately NOT gating `success`, because a save with nothing dirty to write also leaves the mtime alone and that is not a failure. WARNING: with `filename` this is a SaveAs that DUPLICATES: the editor stays on the old map, the new one becomes a resident world (which then makes load_level refuse), and a SECOND save to the same filename opens a modal that freezes the editor -- treat filename as one-shot per name per session.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filename` | string | no | Optional. A /Game asset path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Foo) or a disk .umap path; both accepted and resolved. Omit it to save the level in place -- that is the branch that just works. Passing one is a SaveAs: duplicate + resident world + the one-shot rule above. |
| `save_as` | string | no | Accepted for wire compatibility and IGNORED: the branch is chosen by whether `filename` was given. It comes back inside `requested` to mark it as your input, not a measurement. |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool, error?: string, data?: { saved_filename?: string, saved_package?: string, saved_disk_path?: string, level_name?: string, file_exists_on_disk: bool, file_size_bytes: int, file_existed_before: bool, file_mtime_changed: bool (the write itself -- see the read-only note above), save_call_returned: bool, rescued_with_save_packages: bool, pie_was_stopped: bool, orphan_world_risk?: bool, requested?: { filename?: string, save_as?: bool } } }`

## `select_actors`

*Destructive.*

Select actors by name in the editor viewport/outliner, appending to or replacing the current selection, and report which ones were not found. Use it to stage the input for the selection-driven tools (copy_actors with copy_selected, move_actors_to_level) or to show the user what you mean before they look. WARNING: matches INTERNAL names only (no editor labels) and misses are reported in not_found_names instead of failing, so check not_found_count. Editor world only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_names` | array | yes | Array of internal actor names (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Editor labels do NOT resolve here; convert them with find_actors_by_name. |
| `add_to_selection` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default TRUE = append to whatever is already selected). Pass false to clear the selection first and end up with exactly these actors. |

**Returns:** `{ selected_actors: [actor JSON], selected_count: int, not_found_count: int, not_found_names?: [string], add_to_selection: bool }`

## `set_actor_transform`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move, rotate and/or scale ONE actor (omitted components are left as they are) and return the actor's re-read transform plus the identity of the world that was written. Undoable, and it calls Modify() first -- which matters, because moving an actor from Python does NOT dirty its OFPA package and then save_level reports success while writing nothing. Takes a `world` selector, so it also reaches a LIVE PIE pawn (an editor-only lookup would answer "Actor not found" for an actor that exists in another world). Use set_actor_transforms for many actors, place_actor_on_terrain to drop one onto the landscape.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel), case-insensitive whole-string match. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional: "editor" (default) \| "pie" \| "server" \| "client" \| "pie:N". In co-op the authoritative pawn lives on the server, and a move written to the client world will be corrected by replication. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional new WORLD location, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Absolute, not a delta; any other value (an object, another length) is an error and the actor is not touched. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional new WORLD rotation as the array [pitch, yaw, roll] -- note index 2 is ROLL, not yaw -- or, unambiguously, the object {"pitch":..,"yaw":..,"roll":..}, which is the recommended form. |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional new WORLD scale, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Any other value (an object, another length) is an error and the actor is not touched. |

**Returns:** `{ actor JSON via DescribeActorObject, transform RE-READ off the actor after the write }`

## `set_actor_transforms`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move/rotate/scale MANY actors in a single undoable transaction, each with its own optional location/rotation/scale, reporting success_count, failure_count and the names that did not resolve. Cheaper and atomically undoable versus N set_actor_transform calls. Calls Modify() per actor so their OFPA packages dirty and save_level actually writes them. Takes the same `world` selector as set_actor_transform, so it reaches a live PIE world too. WARNING: resolves the INTERNAL name only (no editor labels, unlike set_actor_transform); a name it cannot find is counted in failure_count, not raised as an error -- read that number.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_transforms` | array | yes | Array of objects {actor_name: internal GetName; location?: [x,y,z] array only; rotation?: [pitch,yaw,roll] or the safer {pitch,yaw,roll}; scale?: [x,y,z] array only}. Omitted components keep their current value; an entry with no actor_name just increments failure_count, and a malformed vector silently reads as zero. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional: "editor" (default) \| "pie" \| "server" \| "client" \| "pie:N". The response stamps which world answered. |

**Returns:** `{ success_count: int, failure_count: int (unresolved or malformed entries -- check it), updated_actors: [actor JSON re-read after the write], failed_actors?: [string], world_name, world_package, ... }`

## `set_allow_cinematic_control`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set whether the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first) may be possessed by cinematic tools such as Sequencer to preview sequences (FEditorViewportClient::SetAllowCinematicControl). It sets the given value rather than toggling; it lasts for this editor session, nothing is saved or undoable, and no viewport is an error. allows_cinematic_control is read back from the viewport. Read the flag without changing it with get_viewport_state (allows_cinematic_control).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow` | boolean | yes | True to allow cinematic control, false to block it |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: bool, allows_cinematic_control: bool }`

## `set_camera_speed`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the camera movement speed of the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first). Affects this editor session only and saves nothing. Returns requested and camera_speed, the value read back from the viewport afterwards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speed` | number | yes | Camera speed as a positive float; 0 or less is an error. Compare camera_speed in the reply to see what the viewport kept. |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: number, camera_speed: number }`

## `set_current_level`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Choose which sub-level of the editor world is CURRENT, i.e. where newly spawned or pasted actors will land. Set it before spawn_actor / paste_actors when a map is split into streaming sub-levels, otherwise everything piles into whichever level happens to be active. Errors honestly if the named streaming level is not loaded/visible; already_current:true when it was already the one. Use move_actors_to_level to relocate actors that ended up in the wrong one.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level_name` | string | yes | "persistent" for the persistent level, or the SHORT name of a loaded, visible streaming sub-level (not a /Game path). |

**Returns:** `{ current_level: string, changed: bool, already_current: bool, success: true } -- current_level is the level current after the call; a level that is not found, or not loaded and visible, is an error instead.`

## `set_cvar`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Sets a console variable via IConsoleManager and reads the value back.  Uses IConsoleManager::Get().FindConsoleVariable(name)->Set(value, ECVF_SetByConsole). Honest error if the named cvar does not exist (unlike a raw console Exec which silently no-ops).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Console variable name, e.g. "r.ScreenPercentage", "r.Shadow.MaxResolution". |
| `value` | any | yes | New value (string, number, or bool; coerced to the cvar's type). |

**Returns:** `{ set: bool, requested_value: string, name: string, value: string, string_value: string, int_value: int, float_value: float, bool_value: bool, help: string, flags: int, set_by: string }`

## `set_cvars_from_json`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Apply many cvars in one call. JSON shape: {"name":"value", ...}

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cvars` | string | yes | JSON object string {"cvar":"value", ...} |

**Returns:** `{ applied, requested, errors: [{name, error}] }`

## `set_engine_ini_value`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write one key into the GConfig copy of an INI (Engine by default), flush it to the saved config under Saved/Config/&lt;Platform>/, and verify by reading it back (applied). It does not edit Config/Default*.ini, and objects that already loaded their config are not reloaded. The value may be text, a bool or a number; with plugin_name it writes a plugin's setting, the section defaulting to the plugin's /Script/&lt;Plugin>.&lt;Plugin>.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | Key inside the section, e.g. "r.DefaultFeature.AntiAliasing"; its current value is replaced. |
| `value` | any | yes | Value to write: a string written verbatim (an empty string is allowed), a JSON bool written as GConfig writes one ("True"/"False"), or a JSON number written as its text (an integer without decimals). |
| `section` | string | no | INI section, e.g. "/Script/Engine.RendererSettings"; created when missing; surrounding brackets are dropped. Required unless plugin_name is given. |
| `config_file` | string | no | Config base name without extension, e.g. "Engine" (default), "Game", "Input"; "Engine.ini" is not resolved. |
| `plugin_name` | string | no | Optional plugin, as its .uplugin is named: an unknown one fails with nothing written; a known one adds its identity to the reply and makes section default to /Script/&lt;Plugin>.&lt;Plugin>. |

**Returns:** `{ applied, section, key, value, value_type: "string"|"bool"|"number", readback_value, config_file, config_file_path, plugin_name?, plugin_status?, plugin_version?, plugin_description?, plugin_author?, plugin_category?, plugin_loaded?, plugin_enabled?, plugin_path?, plugin_file? }`

## `set_enum_bitflags`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Toggle the "bitflags" meta on a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum) so its enumerators can be combined as bit flags.  Idempotent: re-setting the same state reports already_set with applied=false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum). |
| `bitflags` | boolean | yes | Desired state: true to mark as bitflags, false to clear. |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, bitflags: bool, already_set: bool, applied: bool }`

## `set_far_clip_plane`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Override the far clip plane distance, in cm, of the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first, so objects beyond it are culled from the view; no viewport is an error. 0 or a negative distance drops the override and the default far plane applies again. It lasts for this editor session with no undo step and no save, and the previous value is not returned. far_clip_plane is the stored override read back, which is the distance sent, and override_active is true only for a distance above 0. get_viewport_state reads the near plane together with this override (far_clip_plane_override); the near plane is set_near_clip_plane.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `distance` | number | yes | Far clip distance in cm; 0 or any negative value clears the override and the default far plane applies |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: number, far_clip_plane: number, override_active: bool }`

## `set_game_view`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Turn Game View on or off on the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first (the view the editor's G key toggles); no viewport is an error. Turning it on swaps the viewport's show flags for the game set, hiding editor-only chrome such as sprites, the transform widget and selection outlines, and keeps the editor set to put back when it is turned off. It sets the given state, so a repeat call changes nothing; it lasts for this editor session with no undo step and nothing saved. in_game_view is read back. Single flags are set_show_flag, render modes set_viewport_view_mode; to run the game use start_play_in_editor.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | True to enable game view, false to revert to editor view |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: bool, in_game_view: bool }`

## `set_near_clip_plane`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Override the near clip plane distance, in cm, of the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first; no viewport is an error. A negative distance (-1 by convention) drops the override so the engine near plane, GNearClippingPlane, applies again; a distance of at least 0.001, the smallest the editor's Near View Plane control allows, becomes the override. 0 (a degenerate projection), anything else below 0.001 and a value too large for a float are errors before anything changes. It lasts for this editor session with no undo step and no save, and the previous value is not returned. near_clip_plane is the effective near plane read back and override_active says whether an override is now set. get_viewport_state reads both clip planes (near_clip_plane, far_clip_plane_override); the far plane is set_far_clip_plane.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `distance` | number | yes | Near clip distance in cm, at least 0.001; any negative value (-1 by convention) clears the override and falls back to GNearClippingPlane |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: number, near_clip_plane: number, override_active: bool }`

## `set_plugin_enabled`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Turn a plugin on (or off, with enabled=false) in the .uproject and save the project file to disk. WARNING: `enabled` echoes the requested state once the .uproject write succeeded, and the plugin's MODULES are not loaded or unloaded by this call -- the editor has to be restarted before an enabled plugin's classes, assets or MCP tools actually exist, and a disabled plugin's classes keep working until then. So do not treat a following "class not found", or a still-working feature, as a failure of this command; check project_saved and then restart. A plugin the .uproject already has in that state is a no-op: project_saved=false and nothing saved; a .uproject that cannot be saved makes success false. A name this editor has not discovered as a plugin is an error, and nothing is written to the .uproject. WARNING: disabling a plugin whose assets are referenced leaves those references broken on the next start; check get_plugin_status and the referencers first. Use get_plugin_status to read the current state.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin_name` | string | yes | Plugin name exactly as in its .uplugin file (e.g. 'PythonScriptPlugin'), not a path. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true): true enables the plugin, false disables it. |

**Returns:** `{ plugin_name: string (the plugin's own spelling), enabled: bool (the requested state, set when the .uproject write succeeded), project_saved: bool, note: string about the required restart, or that nothing changed }`

## `set_scalability_quality`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Sets engine scalability quality via the Scalability API and reads it back.  Modifies a Scalability::FQualityLevels (starting from the current live state), then applies it with Scalability::SetQualityLevels + ApplyCachedQualityLevels.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quality` | any | no | Level 0-3(/4) or one of "Low"/"Medium"/"High"/"Epic"/"Cinematic". |
| `category` | string | no | Optional category name: "ViewDistance", "AntiAliasing", "Shadows", "GlobalIllumination", "Reflection", "PostProcess", "Texture", "Effects", "Foliage", "Shading", "Landscape", or "all" (default all). |

**Returns:** `{ set: bool, requested_level: int, category: string, ResolutionQuality: int, ViewDistanceQuality: int, AntiAliasingQuality: int, ShadowQuality: int, GlobalIlluminationQuality: int, ReflectionQuality: int, PostProcessQuality: int, TextureQuality: int, EffectsQuality: int, FoliageQuality: int, ShadingQuality: int, LandscapeQuality: int }`

## `set_show_flag`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set one engine show flag (Grid, Bounds, Collision, Wireframe, Lighting...) on the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first; no viewport is an error. It sets the given state rather than toggling: enabled true turns the flag on, false turns it off, and a repeat call changes nothing. flag_name is matched without case against the engine's show flags and registered custom flags; an unknown name is an error before anything changes. It lasts for this editor session, with no undo step, nothing saved and the earlier value not returned. value is the flag read back and flag_index its engine index. get_viewport_state reads Grid, Bounds, Collision, Wireframe and Lighting back; set_game_view swaps the whole flag set; set_viewport_view_mode changes the render mode.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flag_name` | string | yes | Engine show flag name as FEngineShowFlags spells it, e.g. Grid, Bounds, Collision, Wireframe, Lighting; matched without case |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | True to set the flag, false to clear it |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, flag_name: string, flag_index: int, requested: bool, value: bool }`

## `set_struct_member_default`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the default value of a user-defined struct member (read-modify-write; the value is validated against the member's type by the engine, so an incompatible value is an honest error).  Idempotent: re-setting the same value is a no-op success.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `struct_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedStruct. |
| `member_name` | string | yes | Member to edit, by its display name (or internal var name). |
| `default_value` | string | yes | New default as a string appropriate to the member's type (e.g. "7", "true", "1.5", "Hello"); pass "" to clear. |

**Returns:** `{ struct_path: string, member_name: string, default_value: string, applied_default_value: string, already_set: bool, applied: bool, member: object }`

## `set_undo_barrier`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Drop a floor in the undo stack at the current position so no later undo can cross it -- the way to protect everything done SO FAR (yours or the human's) before starting a risky batch that you may want to unwind. Idempotent: a barrier already sitting at the cursor is not pushed twice (already_existed:true). Lift it with remove_undo_barrier (all=true lifts every barrier).

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ success: bool (hardcoded), already_existed: bool (true = nothing new was pushed), undo_barrier: int (cursor it sits at), undo_count: int, queue_length: int }`

## `set_view_type`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Switch the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first, to the perspective camera or one of the six orthographic views; no viewport is an error. type is matched without case, and any other name is an error before anything changes. Switching to an orthographic view unlocks an actor the viewport was piloting, and each projection re-applies the view mode it keeps for itself. It sets the given type, so a repeat call changes nothing; it lasts for this editor session with no undo step and no save. view_type and view_type_index are read back. Read it with get_viewport_state (view_type); render modes are set_viewport_view_mode, the camera position set_viewport_camera.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes | View type name. One of: Perspective, Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Front, Back. Matched without case. |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: string, view_type: string, view_type_index: int }`

## `set_viewport_camera`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Place the camera of the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first) at an absolute world location and/or rotation; at least one is required and no viewport is an error. Editor view only, not undoable or saved: a PIE player camera (set_view_target) or a camera actor (set_camera_transform) does not move. location must be an [x, y, z] array of three numbers in cm and rotation three numbers or a roll/pitch/yaw object; anything else is refused before the camera moves. The reply reads location and rotation back, rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll]. Frame an actor with focus_viewport.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] world location |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, location_set: bool, rotation_set: bool, location: [number], rotation: [number] }`

## `set_viewport_exposure`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the exposure of the active level editor viewport: fixed at ev100 when fixed is true, automatic eye adaptation when false. Affects the viewport only and saves nothing. Returns applied, fixed and ev100 as read back; get_viewport_state reads them (exposure).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fixed` | boolean | yes | True for fixed exposure (use FixedEV100), false for automatic eye-adaptation |
| `ev100` | number | yes | EV100 value to use when fixed=true (any float; typical range -3..20) |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, fixed: bool, ev100: number }`

## `set_viewport_fov`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the perspective field of view, in degrees, of the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first; no viewport is an error. fov must lie in 5..170, the range of the editor's Field of View control, and a value outside it is an error before anything changes. Like that control it sets both the current view FOV and the stored one that a camera reset or the end of a PIE session restores; fov and stored_fov are read back, and an orthographic view ignores them. There is no undo step and no asset is saved, and the previous FOV is not returned. A viewport piloting a camera actor keeps showing that camera's FOV until it stops piloting it. Read it with get_viewport_state (fov); a camera actor's own FOV is set_camera_fov.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fov` | number | yes | Field of view in degrees, from 5 to 170 (the range of the editor's FOV slider) |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: number, fov: number, stored_fov: number }`

## `set_viewport_realtime`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Enable or disable realtime rendering on the active editor viewport

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | True to turn on realtime updates, false to turn them off |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: bool, realtime: bool, effective_realtime: bool, override_active: bool, override_source: string }`

## `set_viewport_view_mode`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the rendering view mode (Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, ShaderComplexity...) of the active level editor viewport, the focused one or else the first; no viewport is an error. view_mode is matched without case. An unknown name is an error before anything changes, and so is a mode the editor only enters with a choice of what to show (a buffer, a visualization, texture streaming data, a zebra direction): the error says which. The mode is stored for the viewport's current projection only (perspective and orthographic keep separate modes) and lasts for this editor session: no undo step, nothing saved. view_mode and view_mode_index are read back, view_mode as the name get_viewport_state reports and this tool takes back. Show flags: set_show_flag; projection: set_view_type; game view: set_game_view.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view_mode` | string | yes | Engine view mode name, matched without case, e.g. Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, CSGWireframe, DetailLighting, LightingOnly, LightComplexity, ShaderComplexity, LightmapDensity, Reflections, PlayerCollision, MeshLODColoration, QuadOverdraw, Clay; each is the engine display name without spaces. BrushWireframe is accepted for Wireframe, ReflectionOverride for Reflections, RandomColor for Random; PathTracing only where ray tracing is allowed. |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: string, view_mode_index: int, view_mode: string }`

## `show_notification`

*Additive.*

Show a transient toast in the editor through the Slate notification manager: message, an optional completion state icon and a lifetime in seconds, after which it fades on its own. completion_state is matched without case, and anything other than Pending, Success or Fail shows no state; the reply echoes it as sent, not as applied. Each call shows another toast, so it is not idempotent, and nothing else changes: no asset, log line or undo step. shown is false when the notification manager returned no toast, and the call still succeeds. An empty or missing message is an error. For a record that stays use print_to_output_log or add_message_log_entry.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | yes | The text to display in the notification; empty is an error. |
| `completion_state` | string | no | Completion state, case-insensitive: "None" (default), "Pending", "Success" or "Fail"; any other value counts as "None". |
| `duration` | number | no | Notification lifetime in seconds before it fades (default 4.0); the value is not validated. |

**Returns:** `{ shown: bool, message: string, completion_state: string, duration: float }`

## `snap_actor_to_ground`

*Destructive.*

Drop ONE editor-world actor straight down until its bounds bottom rests on whatever is below -- meshes, BSP or the landscape. It line-traces first and, because headless traces routinely MISS the landscape, falls back to sampling the heightmap so the actor still lands; sampled_from tells you which path answered. Use place_actor_on_terrain when the ground is definitely the landscape and you want no trace at all, place_actors_on_terrain for many actors.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Name of the actor to snap (editor world). |
| `trace_distance` | number | no | Optional downward trace distance in cm; defaults to 10000 |
| `align_to_surface` | boolean | no | When true, rotate actor to match the surface normal (trace hits only; the heightmap fallback has no normal); defaults to false |
| `fallback_heightmap` | boolean | no | When true (default) and the downward line trace misses (headless traces routinely miss the landscape), fall back to sampling the landscape heightmap at the actor's XY (same sampler as place_actor_on_terrain) so the actor still lands. Set false to require a real trace hit. |

**Returns:** `{ actor: actor JSON, hit: bool, landed: bool, sampled_from: 'trace'|'heightmap', hit_actor?: string, hit_distance?: number }`

## `spawn_actor`

*Additive.*

Place a BUILT-IN engine actor (StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight, SkyLight, CameraActor, Character) into the editor level or a live PIE world, at an optional location/rotation/scale, optionally seeding a light's intensity and color, and return the created actor's JSON. Only these types: for a Blueprint class use spawn_blueprint_actor. Refuses when an actor of that name already exists (omit name to let the engine pick a unique one), and the spawn is undoable. It creates the actor in MEMORY only -- save_level (with the .umap writable) is what puts it on disk. WARNING: with 2+ PIE clients world='pie' can land in the CLIENT world, producing an actor the authority never sees -- ask for world='server' instead, and check the reply's world_package/net_mode to see where the actor actually went.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes | One of StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight, SkyLight, CameraActor, Character (case-insensitive); a light also by its short name Point, Spot, Directional, Rect or Sky. Anything else is a clean error; Blueprints go through spawn_blueprint_actor. |
| `name` | string | no | Optional internal name (and label) for the new actor; must be unused in the target world or the call is refused. When omitted the engine names the actor uniquely and the label is the class default. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional world location, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]; the origin when omitted. Any other value (an object, another length) is an error and nothing is spawned. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional world rotation as the array [pitch, yaw, roll] -- note index 2 is ROLL, not yaw -- or, unambiguously, the object {"pitch":..,"yaw":..,"roll":..}, which is the recommended form. Defaults to zero. Directional, spot and rect lights shine along its forward axis. |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional world scale, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Defaults to 1,1,1; any other value (an object, another length) is an error and nothing is spawned. |
| `static_mesh` | string | no | Optional UStaticMesh asset path, only honoured for type=StaticMeshActor (e.g. /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube). |
| `intensity` | number | no | Optional, light types only: the light component's Intensity in the light's units (Directional: lux; Sky: a multiplier); engine default when omitted. Sent for a non-light type it is refused and nothing is spawned. |
| `color` | array | no | Optional, light types only: [r, g, b] linear color, usually 0..1; engine default (white) when omitted. Sent for a non-light type it is refused and nothing is spawned. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector for WHERE the actor is spawned: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'game' (alias of 'pie') \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- what you want for anything replicated) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N'. Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent spawn into the editor world. |

**Returns:** `{ actor JSON via DescribeActorObject: name, class, location, rotation, scale, plus world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int, light_intensity?: number (light types: the intensity now on the component), light_color?: [r, g, b] (light types: the color now on the component) }`

## `undo`

*Destructive.*

Step the editor's undo stack back by one transaction, or by `count` of them, and report what is left, including next_undo (the label of the entry now on top). WARNING: `success` is ALWAYS true, including when there was nothing to undo -- the real oracle is `applied`, and with a count compare actually_undone against requested (the stack ran out, or an undo barrier stopped it); the honest verification is re-reading whatever you changed. Read get_undo_state first to look before you leap.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | number | no | Optional. How many transactions to undo, at least 1 (default 1); stops early when the stack runs out or reaches an undo barrier. Below 1 is refused. |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool (THE oracle -- false means nothing was undone), requested: int, actually_undone: int (compare against requested), undo_count: int, can_undo: bool, next_undo: string (label of the next entry) }`
